Here's how to adjust Apple AirPods for small ears

By Kamali

People with small ears can often get a better AirPods fit by adjusting how the earbuds sit, trying smaller ear tips on AirPods Pro, running Apple's built-in fit test, or using foam tips. Standard AirPods without tips offer fewer options, so some users may be better off with a Pro model.

AirPods are among the most popular wireless earbuds, but they do not fit every ear equally well. People with small ears or narrow ear canals often find that the earbuds feel loose, fall out or fail to block outside noise. An Engadget guide published in November 2026 explains how to improve the fit, and the right approach depends on which AirPods you own.

If you have standard AirPods without ear tips

Standard AirPods have no tips, so your options are limited. The main method is to push the earbud gently into your ear and rotate the stem toward your face until it locks in place. Engadget notes that people with small ear canals may find it hard to get the tight fit they need. If that applies to you, regular AirPods might not be the best choice, and some users get a better result by moving to AirPods Pro.

If you have AirPods Pro

AirPods Pro come with silicone ear tips in several sizes, which gives you much more room to adjust. The number of sizes depends on the generation. The first-generation AirPods Pro include small, medium and large tips. The second generation adds an extra-small size. The AirPods Pro 3 go further and include an extra-extra-small tip, which can help people with particularly small ear canals. The tips attached when you first open the box are medium.

Choosing the right size is not always obvious. A smaller tip is not automatically the best choice for a small ear, so it is worth trying every size in the box.

Run Apple's fit test

Apple has a built-in test that checks whether your tips create a good seal. Put the AirPods Pro in your ears, open Settings on your iPhone, choose your AirPods and tap the ear tip test. It is called Ear Tip Fit Test or Test Acoustic Seal, depending on the model. Tap Continue and then Play. You will hear a short piece of music, and the result will tell you whether you have a Good Seal or whether you should adjust the buds or try a different size.

If the result is poor, reposition the earbuds, try the test again, and then switch to another tip size and repeat it. Some guides suggest tilting the buds so they sit more vertically in your ears. You can also play bass-heavy music as a quick check. A good seal makes the bass sound fuller.

Changing the tips

Swapping tips takes only a few moments. You pull the old tip off and press the new one onto the earbud until it clicks into place. Follow Apple's instructions for your specific model, since the connector changed on the AirPods Pro 3. Accessories made for earlier models may not fit correctly, and tips from the first-generation AirPods Pro are not designed to be interchanged with the second generation, according to Apple.

Consider foam tips

Some people with small or unusually shaped ear canals find foam tips more comfortable and secure. Foam is soft and pliable, and it is typically squeezed before you put it in your ear so that it expands to fit. Apple introduced foam-infused tips with the AirPods Pro 3, but Engadget says pure foam tips may still work better for some people. Third-party tips can be a good option, but check that they are made for your exact AirPods model, and be cautious about unmarked listings.

When to consider a different model

If you have tried every size and still cannot get a secure fit, the problem may be the design and not the tips. Engadget says some users may achieve a better fit by upgrading to AirPods Pro. For people with the smallest ear canals, the extra-extra-small tips on the AirPods Pro 3 may help, though this is not guaranteed.

What is still unknown

Fit is personal, and there is no exact science to it. What works for one person may not work for another, and tip availability and test names vary by model and software version.

Why it matters

A poor fit affects more than comfort. Earbuds that do not seal properly lose bass, let in more noise and make noise cancellation less effective. Spending a few minutes on the fit can noticeably improve how your AirPods sound.
